findings.problem: The lanes' own documented fresh-root remedy is unreachable, and the failure is a silent green. tui-mount.mjs:124 runs gateTuiPrereqs(...) BEFORE the --install block at :126, and gateTuiPrereqs (lib/tui-lane.mjs:370-377) calls process.exit(0) with a 'SKIP absent-fixture' marker. So `tui-mount --sandbox-root <fresh> --install` — exactly the command the lane's own PREREQ line and the shared remedy text advertise — exits 0 having installed nothing and produced no evidence.
findings.consequence: A reviewer who satisfies F9 (clean root) and follows the lane's printed remedy gets exit 0 and zero artifacts; a green exit code here proves nothing. It also makes F9 and the lane's remedy mutually unsatisfiable as shipped, which is why this task had to install the profile itself.
findings.requiredFix: Run the prereq gate AFTER the --install block (or treat --install as satisfying the fixture prereq), and make a SKIP that would have been fixable by --install a non-zero outcome — a silent exit 0 must not be the signal for 'no evidence produced'.

findings.owner: host-side (NOT our plugin); disclosure owned by t23/t5
findings.problem: The tuiRenderers transcript row does not render: 6 of 7 seam surfaces render, the log-only mpd-tui/board-opened event IS in the durable store, and the scene header itself reports 0 transcript row(s). Independently falsified against the host: a SECOND, independent plugin (my canary, composed only through the sandbox profile's own patch layer) entered apply, its deferred ctx.inject(['tuiRenderers']) callback fired, the service was reachable, register() returned a function without throwing — and still NO transcript row appeared, while the board scene (boardTitleRendered) and our status line rendered in the same run.
findings.supportingSourceEvidence: installed payload @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui@0.10.1 lib/types/dsh-adapter/channel.js:189 gives tuiSettingsSections a local fallback (getLocalSettingsSectionsHost, issue #557) while :195 captures tuiRenderers once with NO fallback; renderers.js keys its WeakMap by the runtime instance and getHostRenderers returns undefined on a miss.
findings.consequence: The surface is NOT CLAIMED (host-side projection gap) and I could NOT produce a row, so the finding does NOT flip back to a plugin defect. NOT fully settled: whether the captured runtime is undefined at channel construction (H1) or the host refuses/never projects plugin registrations (H2) — the host is READ-ONLY for us and exposes no read-back, so the discriminator is UNVERIFIED and both readings are host-side.
findings.requiredFix: Keep the NOT CLAIMED disclosure; the honest end-user-facing statement is 'the renderer row may not appear on this host build'. Our side already reports requested (never confirmed) — see src/renderers.ts outcome(). Upstream: give the renderer path the same local-fallback treatment as tuiSettingsSections, or expose a read-back.

findings.problem: The host's effect ledger cannot witness seam registrations in this composition: it contains only `command` records (36 in my run, all pluginId 'undeclared'), while scenes/status/shortcuts/renderers/themes registrations DO record to tuiEffectLedger in the installed source. So ctx.get('tuiEffectLedger') is not reachable from the extensions-row registration path.
findings.artifact: .mpd/recon/qa/t8-reviewer-20260915T063140Z/home/.dsh-tui/effect-ledger.jsonl (36 × kind:command only) + the host descriptor pane evidence/tui/lanes/2026-09-15T06-26-38.862Z/plugins-descriptor.pane.txt
findings.consequence: The absence of renderer records in the ledger is NOT evidence of a failed registration — I explicitly refused to use it as such. Anyone planning to cite the ledger as a registration witness for the TUI seams would be building on a false negative.
